correctness.rationale: For each proposed p=1,...,11, period-p equations are exactly the union across all \(2^p\) sign vectors of rational affine linear systems with closed sign inequalities. Exact Fraction row reduction and exact Fourier-Motzkin elimination, whose projection rule is elementary and lossless, decide every real feasibility cell including boundaries. All feasible nonsingular points at 5 and 11 are rational and deduplicated by actual cyclic state equality, while a direct six-cycle witness supplies p=6. Direct nonzero-branch Jacobian products give return traces 1,3,-5,+5 and determinant one. Full finite checker and actual output are attached; no extrapolation beyond 11.

originality.rationale: A directly comparable 2009 full-text study gives the general recurrence and periods two/three, without the exact global short-period orbit census. The named MathWorld source prints one outer period-five cycle, while the exact global calculation finds two (one with hyperbolic trace 3); two hyperbolic eleven-cycles and the prime-length gap 7–10 are not provided there. A closely related 2025 full paper treats a different dissipative map. The inaccessible founding 1984 text and unindexed older descriptions impose a genuine residual risk, not a proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: Devaney 1984 founding same-map paper could have statements implying the short-period census; complete text was inaccessible despite lawful full-text searches.
The MathWorld phrase unique period-five orbit may be intended only for interiors of five peripheral hexagons; the present claim is global and includes branch-boundary points.
Search cannot exclude unindexed or differently titled reports of the exact period-eleven classes; independent literature review remains needed.

value.rationale: The exact period cutoff 11 detects the first additional primitive period beyond the familiar 5/6 resonance zones, with sharp nonexistence for 7–10. Distinguishing the globally second period-five orbit from the well-documented outer five-cycle identifies a hyperbolic versus elliptic splitting; the two period-eleven hyperbolic multipliers fix the initial finite unstable orbit skeleton. This is a natural finite classification of a standard conservative piecewise-linear homeomorphism, not a parameter-renaming or unmotivated one-off calculation.
